title: Den Building
strapline: A place of our own, made with our own hands.
intent: Building a den is deeply satisfying, whole-body work — lifting, carrying, stretching, tying — that builds real strength and coordination.
Making something big enough to get inside is genuine construction and engineering: what stays up, what falls down, what keeps the rain out.
A den is almost always a shared project, so it's rich in cooperation, negotiation and shared purpose.
The cosy, hidden, den-that's-ours quality gives children a powerful sense of ownership, belonging and calm.
Once built, the den becomes the base for endless imaginative play and storytelling.
implementation: Provide big, open-ended materials — tarps, sheets, crates, planks, pegs, rope, clips — and a good structure to build against (a fence, trees, an A-frame).
Step back and let children plan, argue, build, fail and rebuild — the struggle is the learning.
Support the problem-solving with questions, not answers: 'The roof keeps sliding off — what could hold it on?'
Help with the collaboration: 'You both want to hold that corner — how could you sort it out?'
Feed in the language of building — over, under, tie, lift, higher, support, balance.
Test the den together against a real purpose: will it keep the rain off, is it big enough for three?
Let the finished den become a home, a cave, a shop — and follow the play that grows inside it.
key_questions: What will your den need to stay standing?
The roof keeps falling — what could hold it up?
How can you all work together to build it?
Is it big enough for everyone — how can we check?
What will your den be once it's built?

impact.text: Children lift, carry, stretch, tie and balance, building whole-body strength and coordination.
Children construct a real, large structure, solving how to make it stand and stay up.
Children cooperate, share materials and negotiate roles to build together.
Children persist through collapses and setbacks, rebuilding until the den holds.
Children use positional and building vocabulary as they plan and construct.
Children turn the finished den into a base for rich, sustained imaginative play.

enhancements: Tarps, sheets, blankets and large fabric pieces for walls and roofs.
Crates, planks, poles, an A-frame or a washing line to build against.
Rope, pegs, clips and elastics for fixing and tying.
Cushions, mats and fairy lights to make the finished den cosy.
Props to turn the den into a home, cave, shop or ship.
A rainy-day challenge: build a den that actually keeps you dry.

playing_exploring: Children take on a big, physical, open-ended challenge and make something of their own.
They test what will hold, stretch, tie and stay up.
active_learning: Children persist through collapses and disagreements, staying with the build until it works.
creating_thinking: Children plan the den, solve the structural problems and adapt their design as they go.
